headline: The Financial Stability Board, an international group of financial regulators, has published final guidance urging banks to keep stronger human oversight over AI agents.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: official international guidance, new today, but guidance rather than binding rules.
importance_line: Banks and other financial firms get a template for when an AI agent must ask a person first, which should shape how regulators judge their AI use, though the guidance is not stated to be binding.
summary: Reuters reports, as carried by CNA, that the Financial Stability Board, which sets international standards for finance, published final guidance on 15 Oct 2026 calling for more human oversight of AI agents, including clear risk-based triggers for when an agent must get human approval. The final text strengthens the June draft and drops the idea of treating AI as 'synthetic employees', saying agents 'do not reason like humans' and may read goals in unexpected ways.
notes: Text read on CNA, which carries Reuters' report; credited to Reuters.
